newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sells no T-bills due to lack of demand.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sells no T-bills due to lack of demand.

text.p: Vietnam sold no Treasury bills at a scheduled auction on Wednesday because of a lack of buying interest, a central bank official said.
Earlier the State Bank of Vietnam said it would offer 50 billion dong ($4.49 million) worth of six-month Treasury bills at the auction.
The official said only one institution had bid for bills on Wednesday, and that was at interest rates well above a ceiling set by the Ministry of Finance.
There have been 17 auctions of Treasury stock so far this year, through which a total of 906.4 billion dong of bills and notes have been sold.

After a slide in the first half of the year, interest rates bottomed out due to tighter liquidity in the money market. As a result, bids at Treasury auctions have tended to come in at far higher levels than the Ministry of Finance is prepared to accept.
As a result much less stock has been allocated at recent auctions than the central bank had originally put on offer. This was the first time no stock was sold at all.
The central bank spokesman said the lack of demand for bills could reflect institutions' need for liquidity ahead of the year-end.
Traders say dollar demand has been strong due to the central bank's moves to engineer a very gradual depreciation of the local currency, but added that the dong market was also very tight.
